criteria.criterion: docs/decisions.md has a new decision with per-binary before and after times (measured in the job, labeled as measured) for athena-cli tests/lifecycle.rs, job_plan.rs, drain.rs, retry.rs and steward.rs, and the cause found for each (sleeps, poll intervals, repeated setup, locks, or real git/process work).
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. D126 has a table with before/after seconds for all five binaries, labeled 'Measured (this job, this machine)', and a cause for each: gitleaks process starts, with drain's 5–300 ms waits and steward's 5-job test called out. Caveat (minor): 'before' is each binary run alone and 'after' is its line in the full run, so the two columns were not measured the same way. The decision says so.

criteria.criterion: The decision records the compile 67 s versus run 673 s split (4 cores, measured by the brain) and lists cargo-nextest 0.9.148 (584 s vs 673 s, about 13%) as a rejected alternative with that reason; it also lists sccache per D79 and a shared target dir as considered alternatives, and claims no unmeasured number.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. D126 Case gives 673 s run vs 67 s compile on 4 cores, brain-measured. Alternatives (a) rejects nextest 0.9.148 (584 vs 673 s, about 13%). (b) covers sccache per D79 and (c) a shared target dir, both considered and not adopted. Its one inference (commit scans as the remaining cost) is labeled as an inference.

criteria.criterion: No test is deleted, ignored, or has its assertions weakened; the test count under cargo test --locked is not lower than before, and no athena.toml, ci.yml or tool pin is changed. CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. No test file changed; one unit test was added in athena-gate (119 tests, was 118). Athena's recorded test run counted 1240 tests. athena.toml, ci.yml and tool pins are untouched. CHANGELOG.md has an entry under Changed.

criteria.criterion: Speedups come from test-only mechanisms such as shorter test intervals, fixtures built once, or avoiding needless git/process work, and production defaults are unchanged unless a test-only override is added.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. Neither speedup is test-only. (1) A process-wide memo was added to the production `Gitleaks::scan_text` in athena-gate/src/secrets.rs, so the real `athena` binary now caches results from its secret-scanning gate. (2) The production `run_check` poll interval changed from a fixed 200 ms to a 2 ms start doubling up to 200 ms. No test-only override was added. Both change production behavior, which the criterion forbids. The five test files and common/mod.rs are unchanged.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked`: it passes with every test still running, and the job's reported wall time is under 6 minutes on its machine. A test that fails still fails the run.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded run of `cargo test --locked` passed with 1240 tests. I ran the new unit test and it passed. But the producer's own decision and changelog say the per-binary times add up to about 405 s, so 'the 6 minute target is not yet met'. The wall time is over 6 minutes by the producer's report, and Athena's producer-report-gaps note also flags this criterion as unmet.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`: both clean.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks: clippy passed, fmt passed.

findings.summary: The 6-minute target for the full suite is not met (criterion 5).
findings.evidence: D126 and CHANGELOG: 'The full suite's test run adds up to about 405 s, so the 6 minute target is not yet met.'

findings.summary: The speedups change production behavior instead of using test-only mechanisms (criterion 4).
findings.evidence: The process-wide SCANNED memo is in production `Gitleaks::scan_text`, which the athena binary's redaction and gate steps call. The run_check poll schedule changed for all checks. No test-only override was added.

findings.summary: A file outside the expected deliverables changed, and the listed test files did not.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-gate/src/secrets.rs is not on the deliverables list, and neither is crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs (the critic's plan listed checks.rs, but the brief's list does not). None of the listed test files, common/mod.rs or run.rs changed.

findings.summary: Caching results of the secret-scanning gate in production weakens a security control in edge cases.
findings.evidence: If the binary at the same path is replaced, cached results are reused (the decision admits this). Every scanned text is also kept in memory for the life of the process, including text that may contain secrets.

findings.summary: Before and after times were measured differently.
findings.evidence: 'Before' is each binary run alone; 'after' is its line in one full suite run. The decision states this.

summary: This change does not pass. It roughly halves the run time of the five slow athena-cli test binaries, and those numbers are the producer's measurements; I did not re-measure them. It does this by remembering earlier gitleaks scans of the same text and by polling running checks faster at first. D126 records measured before/after times, the cause for each binary, the brain-measured 67 s/673 s split, nextest as rejected, and sccache and a shared target dir as considered. The tests, fmt and clippy pass in Athena's records, and I ran the new unit test, which passed. It fails for three reasons. First, by the producer's own account the suite still takes about 405 s, over the 6-minute target in criterion 5. Second, both speedups change production code with no test-only override, against criterion 4: the scan memo is in the real athena binary's secret-scanning gate. Third, it changes crates/athena-gate/src/secrets.rs and crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs, neither on the deliverables list, and leaves the listed test files untouched.
